A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Lie Symmetry Net work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are available and sufficiently readable for reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original Black–Scholes numerical experiments in Section 5 and Vašiček operator-combination experiments in Appendix A.4.

after.justification: v3 retains those numerical results and adds training-time measurements, conservation-law variant experiments, nonlinear-PDE comparisons and a Nasdaq 100 market-data example.

M1.justification: The conservation residual, squared symmetry loss and weighted empirical training objective are retained. Arbitrary auxiliary functions and operator combinations were already supported in v2; v3 tests additional choices and equations without documenting a revised solver procedure.

E1.justification: Sections 5.2–5.3 add KdV and Maxwellian tails equations and European call-option pricing using Nasdaq 100 market data. This substantially extends the synthetic financial-PDE coverage. Vašiček experiments already appeared in v2's appendix.

E2.justification: The existing Black–Scholes comparisons retain PINN, IPINN, sfPINN, ffPINN and LPS. Vašiček panels retain PINN and LSN variants. The new KdV and Maxwellian comparisons reuse the existing PINN/LPS comparator set.

E3.justification: v3 introduces cumulative-time comparisons at fixed error thresholds, a 100,000-step auxiliary-function study, and new PDE configurations with four 50-neuron layers and different collocation counts. KdV/Maxwellian setup paragraphs specify 200,000 iterations, although Figure 10 displays only 80,000. Existing Black–Scholes and Vašiček settings are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds the Black–Scholes O1/O2/combined-conservation-law study in Figure 9, training-efficiency analysis in Table 3 and market-prediction case study in Figure 11. Existing LPS weight sweeps and Vašiček operator-combination analyses are retained; the latter moves into Section 5.2.1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars. The added experiments continue reporting individual values and training trajectories without statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 2's original numerical values are unchanged. New results include 885 seconds for LSN versus 1,990 seconds for PINN to reach error 0.007 at r = sigma = 0.2 (Table 3), plus conservation-law variant, KdV, Maxwellian and market-prediction curves in Figures 9–11.

T1.justification: v3 adds the general adjoint-based conservation-law and conserved-vector construction in Definition A.4. Section 4.2 omits v2's explicit data-fitting and total population-risk formulas. The appendix approximation and generalization bounds and proofs are retained under renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the conservation-law-based LSN contribution and the claim of more than an order-of-magnitude error reduction. Broad applicability beyond Black–Scholes was already claimed in v2; the additional experiments support that retained scope.

C2.justification: v3 introduces an explanation that LSN accesses potential, nonlocal and additional local symmetries beyond LPS, and attributes extra information to auxiliary-function choices. It also interprets training-time advantages and suggests supply/demand or external influences as explanations for market-price discrepancies. These substantive interpretations are absent from v2.

D1.justification: v3 supplies network sizes, collocation counts and optimization settings for the new PDE experiments, and identifies OptionMetrics volatility and Yahoo Finance Treasury-yield inputs. The abstract replaces the anonymous code link with a GitHub link. Existing implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting potential/nonlocal symmetries, general conservation laws and market-data option pricing, including Bluman, Pucci and Saccomandi, and Ibragimov (2007). The related-work section largely retains its positioning; duplicate Bai (2022) entries are consolidated rather than removing a distinct work.

P1.justification: Section 5 is reorganized around Black–Scholes, other equations and real market data; the Vašiček experiment moves from the appendix into the main text. Section 4.2 is shortened and wording is locally edited, while most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds timing Table 3 and Figures 9 and 11. The earlier appendix Vašiček plots are restyled and incorporated into Figure 10 alongside new KdV and Maxwellian panels. Existing experimental figures are redistributed across pages, substantially expanding and reorganizing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The timing measurements, nonlinear-PDE tests, market example and general conservation-law construction broaden v2's supporting evidence. However, v3's new Figure 9 interpretation attributes additional information to l(t) and g(t), while its retained Appendix A.4 derivation shows those functions cancel from the residual. The new PDE experiments also omit selected conservation operators and initial/boundary conditions. These useful additions and unresolved consistency and reproducibility problems leave the net quality effect uncertain.
